issues.failure_explanation: The matrices and dual computation use all m sample points, but the distinctness assumption X ∩ T = ∅ is only stated for a set X of the first n+1 sample points. If x_j = t_k for some j > n+1, entries such as 1/(x_j - t_k) are undefined.

issues.overall_effect: The barycentric basis matrices, dual function, KKT lemma, efficient dual computation, duality theorems, and algorithm are not well-defined under the stated assumptions when m > n+1.
issues.title: Sample set X defined with only n+1 nodes instead of m
issues.why_classification: This is a local premise correction; all substantive results survive once the assumption is imposed on all m sample points.

issues.failure_explanation: As displayed, d(w) minimizes over all barycentric coefficients {α_j}, {β_j}, while the interpolation-constrained parameterization requires α_j = β_j for j ≤ ℓ. Without this constraint, the feasible set is strictly larger and can reduce d(w); for example, at a single sample one can choose α_j = f_j β_j to make the objective zero independently of the interpolation condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the constraint α_j = β_j for j ≤ ℓ to the infimum in eq:rat-d, or define d(w) directly through the constrained minimization in eq:dual.
issues.overall_effect: The stated dual function in eq:rat-d is not the dual function for the constrained problem; later results rely on the constrained version in eq:dual.
issues.title: Dual function definition omits the interpolation parameter constraint
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of the definition; the intended constrained dual and subsequent arguments remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, by Theorem \ref{lem:baryrational2}, we know that both the best approximation $\xi^*=p^*/q^*\in \scrR_{(n)}$  of \eqref{eq:bestf}, and the corresponding   $\wtd \xi=\wtd p/\wtd q$ in barycentric formula achieving the minimum $d(\bw)$ can be parameterized by \eqref{eq:baryform}.

issues.failure_explanation: For ℓ > 0, eq:bestf is the unconstrained discrete rational minimax problem. A solution of eq:bestf need not satisfy ξ(t_j)=y_j, so Theorem lem:baryrational2, which requires interpolation, cannot be invoked to parameterize ξ* in the constrained barycentric form used in the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:bestf with eq:baryInterpMinmax, or explicitly assume ξ* is a solution of the interpolation-constrained problem.
issues.overall_effect: The weak duality theorem is stated and proved under the wrong primal problem; downstream strong duality and extreme-point results cite this weak duality statement.
issues.title: Weak duality theorem assumes solution of the unconstrained problem
issues.why_classification: A one-reference correction restores the intended premise and preserves the theorem's conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is for arbitrary sampled data (x_j, f_j), and η∞ is defined using f_j. The complementary-slackness proof instead writes f(x_j); unless f_j = f(x_j), the displayed equality and the termwise inequality needed to obtain complementary slackness are not valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace f(x_j) by f_j in the complementary-slackness calculation and conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of complementary slackness, and hence the dependent extreme-point theorem, is unsupported for general sampled data as written.
issues.title: Strong duality proof uses f(x_j) instead of sampled data f_j
issues.why_classification: This is a local proof correction; the intended theorem remains unchanged.
